full_judgment:
3. The present petitioners, as plaintiffs, filed Title Suit No. 500 of 1983 against the present defendant-respondents in the court of Subordinate Judge, Jhalakati praying for partition of the land described in schedule to the plaint. The case of the plaintiffs, in short, was that the land measuring 8.19 acres appertaining to C.S. Khatian Nos. 59, 12 and 75 originally belonged to two brothers, namely, Abdul Gafur and Ismail Chowkider in equal share. That Sreemati Charu Bala Ghosh and Sree Aswini Kumar Ghosh were the superior land lords of Khatian No. 59 in two annas share each and the said  four annas share of those landlords were put in auction for arrear of rents and the said superior landlords themselves auction purchased the same. Subsequently Abdul Gal, the predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiffs took pattan of the said four annas Share of Khatian No. 59 from the said land-lords by a kabaliyat dated 05.084946 and possessed that land as exclusive owner. That the remaining 12 annas share of the said C.S. Khatian No. 59 and the land of other two S.A. Khatian Nos. 12 and 75 were being possessed by Abdul Gafur and his brother Ismail Chowkider in equal shares. Abdul Gafur died leaving Wife Surjaban, three sons in plaintiff Nos. 1 to 3, three daughters the plaintiff Nos. 4, 5 and Akhimunnessa. Akhimunnessa subsequently died leaving plaintiff Nos. 6 to 10 as her sole heirs. Latter on, Surjaban gifted her share in favour of the plaintiff Nos. 1 to 3 by a heba-bil-ewaj dated 08.04.1976. Thus the plaintiffs are owners in possession of ten annas share in Khatian No. 59 and eight annas share in each of the Khatian Nos. 12 and 75 that the defendants Nos. 1 to 10 are heirs and successors of Ismail Chowkider. They are owning and possessing the remaining of the divisible land described in schedule "Ka" to the plaint. That during S.A. operation Abdul Gafur was ill and bed-ridden and taking that 'advantage Ismail Chowkider got excess land than his actual share recorded in his name and in the name of his son Abdus Sobhan. That the suit land has never been partitioned by metes and bounds amongst its co-sharers. The plaintiffs demanded partition to the defendants on several occasions, but the defendants did not pay any heed to that and thus the plaintiffs have been compelled to institute the suit for partition. 

 4. The defendant Nos. 1 and 2 contested the suit by filing a joint written statement. The material case of these defendants was that the divisible land described in schedule "Ka" to the plaint belonged to Abdul Gafur and Ismail Chowkider in equal shares. That the plaintiff’s case that four annas share of C.S. Khatian No. 59 was sold in auction and the landlord’s auction purchased the same and subsequently, they settled the same with Abdul Gafur only by kabaliyat is not true at all. These defendants pleaded further case to the effect that Abdus Sobhan the predecessor-in-interest of the defendant Nos. 2 to 7 purchased 3.02 acres of land of Khebat No. 113 by kabala dated 08.04.1930. The defendant No. 11, Abu Baker was the owner of 33 decimals of land of D. S. Khatian No. 59 and he sold the said land to Abdul Wahid, Abdul Kader and the defendant Nos. 1 and  2 by kabala dated 06.05.1966. That Ismail Chowkider took pattan of 93 decimals of land under D.S. Khatian No. 69 by dhakilas dated 22.02.1.924. He died leaving son Abdul Gani, the defendant No. 1, Abdus Sobhan-the predecessor-in-interest of the defendant Nos. 3 to 7, daughter Karful Bibi and widows Waturnessa and Thokabajan Bibi. Waturnessa then died leaving sons Abdul Gani, Abdus Sobhan and daughter Karful Bibi. Karful Bibi gifted 1.48½ acres of land in favour of Abdul Wahid, Abdul Kadir and defendant Nos. 1 and 2 by heba-bil-ewaj dated 24.03.1979. Thokabj an Bibi also gifted 84 decimals of land to them by deed of gift dated 17.12.1981. 

 12. It appears that in this suit for partition the main disputed question is whether four annas share of the lands of C.S. Khatian No. 59 was sold in auction for arrears of rent and whether the auction purchaser’s landlords subsequently settled this four annas share with Abdul Gafur the predecessor of the plaintiffs. It appears that both the trial court and the lower appellate court, on consideration of the evidence including the sale certificate, kabaliyat etc. decided that. Abdul Gafur became the sole owner of four annas share of C.S. Khatian No. 59 by virtue of kabaliyat and thus Abdul Gafur was the owner of total 10 annas share in Khatian No.  59. According to the admission of both the contesting parties Abdul Gafur was owner of eight annas share in each of the other two Khatian Nos. 12 and 75 described in schedules to the plaint. The trial court, accordingly, allotted a separate saham for the plaintiffs and the appellate court affirmed that judgment and decree of the trial court. The High Court Division without giving any observation as to this concurrent finding of the courts of facts set aside the judgment of the appellate court below and sent back the appeal on remand with a direction for writing judgment afresh. This has not been proper and justified at all. The judgment of the appellate court is a judgment of affirmance and as such it cannot be discarded for the reason only that it is not an elaborate judgment discussing all the evidence in details. The lower appellate court has given its decision on the material point at issue concurring with that of the trial court. The revisional court if found any error in that decision it could have rejected that decision and given its own decision by writing a full fledged judgment.
